name: Chief petty officer collar device
explanation: The fouled anchor — an anchor with line wrapped around the stock — is how a chief petty officer is recognized on khaki and on some other uniforms. It is the rank mark of an E-7.
criteria: Worn after promotion to chief petty officer. Date of rank here is 16 September 2014.

name: Electronics Technician chief rating badge
explanation: The sleeve or chest badge of a chief who is an Electronics Technician: an eagle, a helium-atom specialty mark (the ET symbol), three chevrons, and one rocker. Gold, rather than red, is worn by a chief with qualifying good conduct. Six Good Conduct Medals are in this record.
criteria: The rating is Electronics Technician. The rocker is added at chief petty officer.

name: Service stripes
explanation: One stripe for each four years of active service. Twenty years and eight months rates five stripes. They are gold because a chief petty officer with good conduct wears gold instead of red. An older shadowbox graphic of this career shows four stripes; five is what the final service length rates. The number can be changed in the profile data.
criteria: Each stripe is four full years. The fifth is earned at twenty years.

name: Joint Communications Support Element device
explanation: The badge of the Joint Communications Support Element, the joint communications unit of the 2009–2015 tour.
criteria: Assignment to the Joint Communications Support Element.
